chapter: Reel IV retellings and New York pianists
title: The 'White Cliffs of Dover' copying story again
summary: He retells how a white trumpet-player bandleader copied the Apollo show's 'White Cliffs of Dover' and recorded it.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: But anyway, we come along a little while later, and this trumpet player -- he just died a few months ago -- did you know him?
Something red ... did he have a band?
Yeah, he had a band.
Was it Erskine Hawkins?
Huh?
It wasn't Erskine Hawkins -- he's not dead.

No. He was a trumpet player and a singer -- oh, what's his name. He died a few months ago, he was in the hospital a long while, and he had that girl who used to sing with him. Anyway, 'White Cliffs of Dover' was a big number and his band was playing it, and he told all of his band men to copy their parts, and he had somebody in the audience take down the lyrics, and Bobby Caston was a singer.
She was the first one I heard do 'God Bless The Child.' I remember her doing it before Billie Holiday.
Yeah, she was before Billie, and she sang The 'White Cliffs of Dover,' and it was a big hit -- and this guy, he made a record.
This guy, this trumpet player?
Yeah, he went down and made a record on this number.
Oh, a black trumpet player?
No, a white player.
Oh. A white player.
Yeah. He was one of the early bands.
Wasn't he -- didn't he just die recently?

No. I thought I'd never miss that guy's name, but anyway, I saw him downtown, and I said, "Oh, you made a record, got a big record out, huh? 'White Cliffs of Dover'?" I said, "It was my number -- all you did was change the endings!" "Ha ha ha ha!" That's all he said.
Was that your number, The White Cliffs of Dover?
No, but as I said, I made the arrangement.
Oh, I see.

And he took -- he had every member in his band copy their part, and he had somebody come in and sit down in the show and take down the lyrics.

Chick Webb used to do that, sure, take my music, and you go up to the Savoy and you'd hear my music. I used to tell Chick about it.
